messages.author: 0e8054b18ece3e51
messages.subject: Structure over multiple variables
parts:
Dear all,

I thought I had a simple problem, but somehow I cannot answer this myself... Instead of having a structure (say "rw1") over 1 variable, I want it over multiple variables. To make it concrete, say I have a continuous Y variable, and three CONTINUOUS X variables. The measurement Eq. is straightforward;
Y = b1X1 + b2X2 + b3X3 + e,

with e being gaussian errors. Again, this is simple enough and can be estimated by INLA or even OLS. However, I want to have the following state Eq;
b1 ~ N(0,5);   # or whatever, has to be largely un-infomative. Where 5 is the std.dev.

for(k = 2:3){    # in reality I have about 10 of these...
   b_{k} ~ b_{k-1} + n;
}

with n ~ N(0,5); # or whatever again.

So I hope you see my issue here, and hopefully I simply missed a simple solution here. I don't have reproducible code, given that I haven't even attempted this yet. (I do know how to do it in Stan/JAGS for example, so I want to know if I can do this first...)
Many thanks, as always,
Alex

messages.author: 0e8054b18ece3e51
messages.subject: Re: Structure over multiple variables
parts:
Just noticed a small mistake.
n_{t-1}; with n ~ N(0,tau_n)
where we estimate tau, which should have a largely uninformative prior. The same goes for e of course.

Also, I do see how one could add additional `fake' observations to get this to work. Instead of having X1, X2 and X3 in the data, you could have 1 X. But you have three entries for every previous 1 observation. (So you also have 3 entries of the same Y.) If you then have a t `index' going from 1 to three alongside X, you could do something like;

f(t, X, model = "rw1", values = seq(1,3,1)).

But I am not sure if this is actually a valid solution or if I get into different issues then. 
Again, thanks in advance!

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Structure over multiple variables
parts:
you can do this with

b1 = rep(1,n)
b2 = rep(2,n)
b3 = rep(3,n)

y ~ -1 + f(b1, X1, model='rw1', values = 1:3, constr=FALSE) +
f(b2, X2, copy = "b1") +
f(b3, X3, copy = "b1")

maybe you want to fix the precision of the first rw1.

this would give a RW1 with length 3, in the the 'fixed effects' as you
describe.
